title: Swallowing Difficulties in Parkinson's
content: Parkinson's disease can affect the muscles and coordination involved in swallowing. Swallowing difficulties may include coughing or choking while eating or drinking, difficulty moving food through the mouth, a sensation that food is sticking, taking longer to eat, or difficulty managing saliva. Swallowing problems can increase the risk of food or liquid entering the airway and can affect nutrition and hydration. A speech-language pathologist can evaluate swallowing and recommend appropriate strategies. New, persistent or worsening swallowing difficulties should be medically evaluated, particularly when choking or difficulty breathing occurs.
